newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to publish harmonised inflation data.
newsitem.headline: EU to publish harmonised inflation data.

text.p: The European Commission releases for the first time on Friday (1100 GMT) harmonised inflation data designed to help to determine which countries qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU).

The so-called harmonised indices of consumer prices will be used when the European Union in early 1998 decides which countries qualify for EMU. Price stability is one of five economic criteria which must be met.
Eurostat, the EU's statistics office, and the national statistics agencies have worked together to harmonise the way inflation is measured to make the figures comparable.
Friday's statistics will cover January and Eurostat will then publish such data every month. The decision on which countries qualify for EMU will be based mainly on data for 1997.
Eurostat will publish figures for all 15 EU countries.

According to the Maastricht treaty, a country's average inflation rate over a year should not exceed by more than 1.5 percentage points that of, at most, the three best-performing member states in terms of price stability.
The harmonised figures may well differ from those published nationally as methods of compilation differ.
For example, the British harmonised figure, released already last month, was 2.2 percent year-on-year in January, much lower than the increase in the official retail price index of 2.8 percent.
Last November, the European Commission estimated that 14 countries had a good chance of meeting the inflation requirement in 1997 -- all member states except Greece.
